correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and nonempty proper S, reverse a decrements the earliest cyclic run start while positive, whereas nonexpanding reverse b cannot decrement it. The first growth therefore costs at least r inverse rotations and one inverse b. The word b a^r attains this bound, and equality forces its uniqueness. A disjoint binary-membership count gives 2^(n-2), (r+1)2^(n-r-2), and n-1 subsets in the three ranges. Independent subset-power BFS checks 4070 cases, and word enumeration verifies 492 uniqueness cases. The finite checks are not substituted for the all-n proof.

evidence: The 2026 certificate establishes a one-sided sufficient condition and shows some Černý subsets are stuck; the new theorem establishes the value E_n(S) for every nonempty proper S and gives a unique optimum and closed count for each threshold.
Preimage complexity theorems concern algorithmic decision problems for arbitrary DFAs, which have different quantifiers and do not specify this exact description for the fixed family.
Forward rank and avoidance profiles of the Černý family concern the image of Q or avoidance of prescribed targets and do not imply the first strictly increasing preimage word for arbitrary S.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Same automaton, same subset variable, and the equivalent preimage definitions were compared, not merely titles. A general algorithm permitting computation of minext is not a theorem asserting its exact symbolic closed form or histogram. The antecedent of Miccinesi’s sufficient condition is not known to cover all subsets, and the paper explicitly allows exceptional subsets.

evidence: Berlinkov, Ferens and Szykuła formulate inverse-image extensibility and bounded-length decision problems, and give one illustrated Černý instance; no all-subset shortest-word formula or histogram was found in the inspected problem statements and proofs.

The new statement can equivalently be formulated as the minimum reverse-path distance in the power automaton to a subset of larger size, or the minimum length of a word strictly shrinking the inverse image of the complement.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: By complementation, the identity (Q minus S) w^{-1}=Q minus (S w^{-1}) shows that strict inverse growth of S is equivalent to strict inverse shrinkage of its complement, not forward-image compression; standard avoidance and total extension are different predicates. The general decision algorithms do not imply the explicit all-subset length distribution without a specialized proof.

The four-state example in the 2017 paper illustrates the definition but does not cover arbitrary n and S. The search result is not itself evidence of nonexistence; an undiscovered earlier formula remains a priority risk.

originality.rationale: Specific primary full texts and equivalent formulations were compared. The 2026 closest paper proves existence of exceptional subsets but not the exact values, unique shortest words or full histogram; the 2017 preimage paper gives general decision complexity and a finite example. An equivalent stronger all-subset classification was not found; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An unpublished or unindexed specialist result might already derive the special-case distribution.
The general-purpose preimage decision algorithms can calculate these lengths on fixed inputs; this work claims a symbolic classification, not algorithmic decidability.
An overlooked equivalent lemma using forward complement wording could dominate the result.

value.rationale: The per-subset shortest inverse-extension length is the natural local invariant underlying the synchronization extension method. Determining every value and unique optimal word for an extremal classical family, together with a complete all-n histogram and exact identification of all n-1 subsets violating the short-extension threshold, sharpens a specifically motivated structural gap in recent certificate work. This is a complete family-wide classification, not a cosmetic variant of a single preimage example or a new claim about general reset bounds.
